MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #17
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What number is the Roman numeral II? (1 mark)
   A. 2
   B. 6
   C. 7
   D. 5

2. Round 379 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 390
   B. 370
   C. 300
   D. 380

3. How many factors does 45 have? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 8
   C. 6
   D. 5

4. Which Roman numeral stands for 3? (1 mark)
   A. III
   B. VX
   C. IIII
   D. VIIII

5. A library has 5,208 story books and 3,796 textbooks. How many books does it have? (1 mark)
   A. 9,004 books
   B. 10,004 books
   C. 9,104 books
   D. 8,994 books

6. What is the rule of the pattern 125, 250, 375, 500? (1 mark)
   A. add 125
   B. add 250
   C. add 175
   D. subtract 125

7. A farmer had 6,500 seedlings and planted 2,875 of them. How many seedlings are left? (1 mark)
   A. 3,615 seedlings
   B. 4,375 seedlings
   C. 3,725 seedlings
   D. 3,625 seedlings

8. What is the next number in the pattern 800, 675, 550, 425, ...? (1 mark)
   A. 300
   B. 675
   C. 425
   D. 175

9. Estimate 8,652 − 3,748 by rounding each number to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 4,900
   B. 4,910
   C. 4,890
   D. 5,000

10. Work out 32 × 21. (1 mark)
   A. 96
   B. 682
   C. 672
   D. 662

11. What does the partial product 36 × 20 equal? (1 mark)
   A. 720
   B. 7,200
   C. 56
   D. 72

12. What is 78 ÷ 6? (1 mark)
   A. 14
   B. 12
   C. 23
   D. 13

13. Change 22/7 to a mixed fraction. (1 mark)
   A. 1 3/7
   B. 3 2/7
   C. 4 1/7
   D. 3 1/7

14. In the fraction 9/11, what does the numerator 9 tell us? (1 mark)
   A. How many of the equal parts are taken
   B. How many equal parts the whole has
   C. The size of each part in centimetres
   D. The number of wholes

15. In the fraction 3/4, which number is the denominator? (1 mark)
   A. 3
   B. 7
   C. 4
   D. 1

16. What is 1/10 of 50? (1 mark)
   A. 11
   B. 10
   C. 45
   D. 5

17. Write 6/100 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 0.6
   B. 0.006
   C. 0.06
   D. 6.0

18. Which is greater, 0.3 or 0.29? (1 mark)
   A. It cannot be told
   B. They are equal
   C. 0.29
   D. 0.3

19. Write 27/100 as a decimal. (1 mark)
   A. 0.27
   B. 0.72
   C. 0.027
   D. 2.7

20. One layer of a cuboid has 12 blocks and there are 2 layers. What is the volume? (1 mark)
   A. 22 blocks
   B. 36 blocks
   C. 24 blocks
   D. 14 blocks

21. Cuboid A is 10 by 2 by 2 blocks (length, width, height). Cuboid B is 5 by 4 by 3 blocks. Which has the greater volume? (1 mark)
   A. It cannot be told
   B. They are equal
   C. Cuboid A
   D. Cuboid B

22. How many 1/2 L bottles can be filled from 12 L of juice? (1 mark)
   A. 18
   B. 24
   C. 12
   D. 6

23. How many 5 L buckets can be filled from a 20 L jerrycan? (1 mark)
   A. 15
   B. 2
   C. 5
   D. 4

24. Which of these is the unit of capacity? (1 mark)
   A. Hour
   B. Kilogram
   C. Litre
   D. Metre

25. How long is a lesson that starts at 10:30 a.m. and ends at 2:15 p.m.? (1 mark)
   A. 4 h 45 min
   B. 3 h 30 min
   C. 3 h 45 min
   D. 3 h 55 min

26. Kip faces North and makes a half turn. Which way does he face now? (1 mark)
   A. North
   B. South
   C. East
   D. West

27. At 6 o'clock the hands of a clock make (1 mark)
   A. a straight line
   B. a right angle
   C. a small angle
   D. no angle

28. How many lines of symmetry does a triangle with three equal sides have? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 2
   C. 3
   D. 4

29. The table shows the type of transport 10 pupils use to come to school: walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1, car 1. How many more are there of walking than of bicycle? (1 mark)
   A. 8
   B. 4
   C. 5
   D. 6

30. The table shows the type of transport 10 pupils use to come to school: walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1, car 1. Which one has the greatest number? (1 mark)
   A. walking
   B. bus
   C. bicycle
   D. car

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. A triangle has sides of 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. Find its perimeter. (2 marks)

32. A trader buys 18 crates with 35 bananas in each crate. How many bananas are there altogether? (3 marks)

33. A rectangular plot is 12 m long and 8 m wide. Peter walks once round the plot. How far does he walk? (3 marks)

34. A tank has 50 L of water. The family uses 18 L. How much water is left? (2 marks)

35. A rectangle is cut into 12 equal parts and 5 parts are shaded. What fraction is shaded and what fraction is not shaded? (2 marks)

36. Arrange 605, 560, 650 and 506 from smallest to largest. (3 marks)

37. A tally chart shows walking 6, bicycle 2, bus 1 and car 1 for 10 pupils. How many pupils walk to school? How many do not walk? (3 marks)

38. State whether 1,468 and 3,975 are even or odd. Give a reason for each. (3 marks)

39. Explain how you can use a beam balance to find the mass of a bag of sugar. (3 marks)

40. A bus leaves at 10:30 a.m. and arrives at 2:15 p.m. How long is the journey? (3 marks)

41. Achieng buys 3 packets of flour of 1/2 kg each and 2 packets of sugar of 1 kg each. Find the total mass. (3 marks)

42. A trader has 800 eggs. Each crate holds 100 eggs. How many crates are needed? (2 marks)

43. A learner says that a half turn is the same as two quarter turns. Is the learner right? Explain. (2 marks)

44. Rectangle P has 5 rows and 7 columns. Rectangle Q has 6 rows and 6 columns. Which has the bigger area and by how much? (4 marks)

45. Explain how a quarter turn is related to a right angle and how four quarter turns are related to a full turn. (3 marks)

46. A ribbon is 1 metre long. Write 27 centimetres as a fraction of a metre and as a decimal. (3 marks)

47. Wafula has 20 goats. One fifth of them are brown. How many goats are brown? Show your working. (3 marks)

48. Divide 47 by 5. Check your answer using multiplication and addition. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #17 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — 2
   II stands for 2.

2. D — 380
   Look at the ones digit 9. It is 5 or more, so go up to the next ten. 379 rounds to 380.

3. C — 6
   The factors of 45 are 1, 3, 5, 9, 15, 45. There are 6 of them.

4. A — III
   3 is written III. Letters after a bigger letter are added.

5. A — 9,004 books
   Add 5,208 + 3,796 = 9,004 books.

6. A — add 125
   Each number is 125 more than the one before it, so the rule is add 125.

7. D — 3,625 seedlings
   Subtract 6,500 − 2,875 = 3,625. Check by adding: 3,625 + 2,875 = 6,500.

8. A — 300
   The rule is subtract 125. 425 − 125 = 300.

9. A — 4,900
   8,652 rounds to 8,650 and 3,748 rounds to 3,750. 8,650 − 3,750 = 4,900.

10. C — 672
   32 × 1 = 32 and 32 × 20 = 640. 32 + 640 = 672.

11. A — 720
   36 × 2 = 72, then × 10 gives 720.

12. D — 13
   6 × 13 = 78, so 78 ÷ 6 = 13.

13. D — 3 1/7
   22 ÷ 7 = 3 remainder 1. The whole number is 3 and the fraction is 1/7, so 22/7 = 3 1/7.

14. A — How many of the equal parts are taken
   The numerator is the top number. In 9/11 it says that 9 parts are taken.

15. C — 4
   The denominator is the bottom number. It shows how many equal parts the whole is cut into.

16. D — 5
   50 ÷ 10 = 5 and 5 × 1 = 5. So 1/10 of 50 is 5.

17. C — 0.06
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 6/100 = 0.06.

18. D — 0.3
   Compare the tenths first. 0.3 is greater than 0.29.

19. A — 0.27
   Tenths need one digit after the decimal point and hundredths need two digits. 27/100 = 0.27.

20. C — 24 blocks
   Volume = blocks in one layer × layers = 12 × 2 = 24 blocks.

21. D — Cuboid B
   A = 10 × 2 × 2 = 40 blocks. B = 5 × 4 × 3 = 60 blocks. Cuboid B is greater.

22. B — 24
   Each litre fills 2 half-litre bottles, so 12 L fills 12 × 2 = 24 bottles.

23. D — 4
   20 ÷ 5 = 4 buckets.

24. C — Litre
   Capacity is measured in litres.

25. C — 3 h 45 min
   Count on from 10:30 a.m. to 2:15 p.m.. The total is 3 h 45 min.

26. B — South
   Going clockwise the order is North, East, South, West. Going anticlockwise it is North, West, South, East. North followed by a half turn gives South.

27. A — a straight line
   At 6 o'clock the hands point in opposite directions, making a straight line.

28. C — 3
   Each line goes from a corner to the middle of the opposite side.

29. B — 4
   6 − 2 = 4.

30. A — walking
   The biggest number is 6, which belongs to walking.

SECTION B
----
31. (2 marks)
   Answer: 12 cm
   Working / marking points: 3 + 4 + 5 = 12. 1 mark for adding all three sides and 1 mark for the unit.

32. (3 marks)
   Answer: 630 bananas
   Working / marking points: 18 × 5 = 90 (1 mark); 18 × 30 = 540 (1 mark); 90 + 540 = 630 (1 mark).

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: 40 m
   Working / marking points: 12 + 8 + 12 + 8 = 40 m. 1 mark for identifying perimeter, 1 mark for the sum, 1 mark for unit.

34. (2 marks)
   Answer: 32 L
   Working / marking points: 50 − 18 = 32. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the unit.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: 5/12 is shaded and 7/12 is not shaded.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 5/12 and 1 mark for 12 − 5 = 7, so 7/12.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: 506, 560, 605, 650
   Working / marking points: Compare hundreds first, then tens. 1 mark for each correct pair of positions, up to 3 marks.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: 6 pupils walk. 10 − 6 = 4 pupils do not walk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 6, 1 mark for 10 − 6, 1 mark for 4.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1,468 is even because it ends in 8. 3,975 is odd because it ends in 5.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct classification with a reason (2 marks) and 1 mark for referring to the ones digit.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Put the sugar in one pan. Add known masses to the other pan until the beam is level. Add up the masses to find the mass of the sugar.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for putting the sugar in a pan, 1 mark for adding known masses until level, 1 mark for adding the masses.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 hours 45 minutes
   Working / marking points: 10:30 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. is 2 h (1 mark); 12:30 to 2:15 p.m. is 1 h 45 min (1 mark); total 3 h 45 min (1 mark).

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 kg
   Working / marking points: 3 × 1/2 = 1 1/2 kg (1 mark); 2 × 1 = 2 kg (1 mark); total 3 1/2 kg (1 mark).

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: 8 crates
   Working / marking points: 800 ÷ 100 = 8. 1 mark for the division and 1 mark for the unit.

43. (2 marks)
   Answer: Yes. A half is made of two quarters, so two quarter turns make one half turn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for yes, 1 mark for the reason.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: Q is bigger by 1 square unit.
   Working / marking points: P = 35 (1 mark); Q = 36 (1 mark); Q is bigger (1 mark); difference 1 (1 mark).

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: A quarter turn makes a right angle. Four quarter turns, that is four right angles, make a full turn.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for quarter turn = right angle, 1 mark for four quarters, 1 mark for full turn.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: 27/100 m = 0.27 m
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying 1 m = 100 cm, 1 mark for 27/100, 1 mark for 0.27.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 goats
   Working / marking points: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 (2 marks) and 1 × 4 = 4 goats (1 mark).

48. (3 marks)
   Answer: 9 remainder 2. Check: 9 × 5 + 2 = 47.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 9, 1 mark for remainder 2, 1 mark for the check.
